# Tart Runner Fleet

> A fail-closed control plane that schedules ephemeral GitHub Actions runners as
> Tart VMs on a single Apple-silicon Mac.

One daemon holds a singleton authority lease, subscribes to GitHub Actions
runner scale sets, clones an immutable Tart VM per queued job, registers a
just-in-time ephemeral runner inside it, and deletes the VM when that job ends.
State is durable SQLite (WAL + operation outbox). Under
`~/Library/Application Support/tart-runner-fleet/`: the binary is
`current/fleet` and the default endpoint is `unix://.../state/fleetd.sock`.

Invariants an agent must respect:

- Read-only commands (`status`, `queues`, `instances`, `operations`,
  `observations`, `health`, `doctor`, `metrics`, `config validate`, `version`,
  `api-version`) are always safe. Parse `-o json` (`apiVersion: fleet.v1`);
  never scrape human tables, `launchctl`, or SQLite.
- Guarded commands (`scale-sets provision --apply --write`,
  `operations discharge`, `update adopt`, `update apply-latest`) need an exact
  `--confirm` token, the two operator mutations also `--reason`, and all are
  refused outside `authority` mode. Run them only under an operational task.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 local failure, 2 usage, 3 not found, 4 unavailable,
  5 degraded/not ready, 6 unsafe precondition. Exit 4 or 5 is evidence, never
  permission to assume zero demand or delete VMs.
- Never hand-edit the state directory (`fleet.json`, `fleet.db*`,
  `installed-generation.json`); never delete a VM without fresh ownership,
  runner, job, Tart, and host evidence.
- Updates are forward-only and quiescence-gated: the 5-minute updater defers
  while any queue, VM, retry, or dead operation exists, and rolls back if the
  new generation does not become ready. A busy-fleet refusal is a success.

## Architecture

- [docs/FLEET_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md](docs/FLEET_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md): target architecture, SLOs, and implementation sequence.
- [docs/adr/0002-official-scale-set-protocol.md](docs/adr/0002-official-scale-set-protocol.md): demand comes from the official scale-set protocol.
- [docs/adr/0003-sqlite-outbox.md](docs/adr/0003-sqlite-outbox.md): SQLite WAL state and idempotent operation outbox.
- [docs/adr/0004-bounded-control-plane-priority.md](docs/adr/0004-bounded-control-plane-priority.md): bounded control-plane scheduling priority.
- [docs/adr/0010-ephemeral-guest-shutdown.md](docs/adr/0010-ephemeral-guest-shutdown.md): the guest powers off when its ephemeral runner exits.
- [docs/adr/0011-atomic-production-updates.md](docs/adr/0011-atomic-production-updates.md): atomic, forward-only production updates.
- [docs/adr/0012-shared-cross-platform-capacity.md](docs/adr/0012-shared-cross-platform-capacity.md): Linux and macOS share one capacity envelope.
- [docs/adr/0021-dischargeable-dead-letters.md](docs/adr/0021-dischargeable-dead-letters.md): a dead letter is parked and operator-dischargeable.
- [docs/adr/0025-saturation-is-not-durable-failure.md](docs/adr/0025-saturation-is-not-durable-failure.md): a saturated host is not evidence of failure.
- [docs/adr/0026-queued-demand-expires-on-proven-absence.md](docs/adr/0026-queued-demand-expires-on-proven-absence.md): queued demand expires only on proven absence.
